zh.caption: 圖 1｜User Flow：客人怎麼完成用餐
zh.description: 箭頭表示這個簡化案例的操作順序。餐廳內部的系統分工留給下一張圖。

items.title: 入座
items.body: 客人找到座位。

items.title: 點餐
items.body: 選擇並送出餐點。

items.title: 等待
items.body: 等候餐點送達。

items.title: 用餐
items.body: 享用餐點。

items.title: 結帳
items.body: 完成付款。

zh.caption: 圖 2｜餐廳資訊系統如何運作（假設範例）
zh.description: 箭頭是資訊傳遞關係：點餐平板→訂單管理系統；訂單管理系統分別傳給廚房、庫存與結帳系統。下方三者是平行接收者，沒有彼此先後關係。

items.title: 點餐平板
items.body: 送出訂單 → 訂單管理系統

items.title: 訂單管理系統
items.body: 接收訂單，分送三類資訊。

items.title: 廚房顯示器
items.body: 訂單管理系統 → 出餐資訊

items.title: 庫存系統
items.body: 訂單管理系統 → 用量

items.title: 結帳系統
items.body: 訂單管理系統 → 金額

zh.caption: 圖 3｜收件資料檢核的 User Flow
zh.description: 填寫→檢查→完整性判斷。否：顯示缺漏→補填或修正→回到檢查；是：預覽→下載 JSON。這是操作條件與回復流程，不是軟體架構。修改輸入會使舊結果失效，匯出前再驗證。

items.title: 填寫收件資料
items.body: 輸入三個必要教學欄位。

items.title: 按下檢查
items.body: 檢查目前輸入。

items.title: 資料完整嗎？
items.body: 依教學完整性規則分成是／否。

items.title: 否：顯示缺漏欄位
items.body: 指出需要補填或修正的地方。

items.title: 補填或修正
items.body: → 回到「按下檢查」，使用更新的輸入。

items.title: 是：預覽結果
items.body: 檢視目前輸入對應的檢查結果。

items.title: 下載 JSON 報告
items.body: 下載前再驗證；完整不代表正式受理。

zh.caption: 圖 4｜Streamlit 程序與資料位置
zh.description: 使用者→瀏覽器；瀏覽器↔Python／Streamlit程序為Streamlit通訊（WebSocket）。rules.py與Session State都位於同一Python程序內；雙向符號表示呼叫／結果或讀寫，不表示獨立服務。JSON下載到使用者裝置。主機分組不代表已驗證的安全信任邊界。

items.title: 使用者
items.body: 操作瀏覽器。

items.title: 瀏覽器：操作介面
items.body: 輸入與結果顯示；↔ Python／Streamlit程序。

items.title: Python／Streamlit 程序
items.body: 執行驗證與報告產生。

items.title: rules.py：驗證規則
items.body: 程序內直接呼叫／回傳結果。

items.title: Session State：工作階段記憶體
items.body: 程序內暫存輸入與已檢查快照；讀／寫。

items.title: 使用者裝置上的 JSON 檔案
items.body: 瀏覽器 → 下載；與伺服器記憶體分開管理。

zh.caption: 圖 5｜C4 架構模型的四個層級
zh.description: 向下箭頭表示逐層放大結構，不表示執行順序。依問題選擇有幫助的層級，不必每次畫完四層。Container不一定是Docker容器。

items.title: C1 · System Context
items.body: 誰使用系統？與哪些外部系統合作？

items.title: C2 · Container
items.body: 有哪些應用程式、服務及資料儲存？

items.title: C3 · Component
items.body: 單一應用程式內有哪些功能組件？

items.title: C4 · Code
items.body: 組件內部有哪些類別、函式與程式碼？

en.caption: Figure 1 | User Flow: how a customer completes a meal
en.description: Arrows show the action order in this simplified example. Internal system responsibilities belong to the next diagram.

items.title: Take a seat
items.body: The customer finds a seat.

items.title: Order
items.body: Choose and submit dishes.

items.title: Wait
items.body: Wait for the meal to arrive.

items.title: Eat
items.body: Enjoy the meal.

items.title: Pay
items.body: Complete payment.

en.caption: Figure 2 | A restaurant information system (hypothetical)
en.description: Arrows show information relationships: ordering tablet → order management; order management separately sends information to kitchen, inventory and billing systems. The three receivers are parallel, not successive steps.

items.title: Ordering tablet
items.body: Order → order management

items.title: Order management
items.body: Receive orders and distribute three kinds of information.

items.title: Kitchen display
items.body: Order management → preparation details

items.title: Inventory system
items.body: Order management → usage

items.title: Billing system
items.body: Order management → amount

en.caption: Figure 3 | User Flow for the intake completeness checker
en.description: Enter → check → completeness decision. No: show omissions → correct → return to Check. Yes: preview → download JSON. These are actions and recovery conditions, not software architecture. Editing invalidates old results; export revalidates.

items.title: Enter intake data
items.body: Enter the three required teaching fields.

items.title: Press Check
items.body: Check the current input.

items.title: Is the data complete?
items.body: Branch on the teaching completeness rules.

items.title: No: show missing fields
items.body: Identify information to supply or correct.

items.title: Supply or correct data
items.body: → Return to Press Check with updated input.

items.title: Yes: preview results
items.body: Inspect results for the current input.

items.title: Download JSON report
items.body: Revalidate before download; completeness is not official intake.

en.caption: Figure 4 | Streamlit processes and data locations
en.description: User → browser; browser ↔ Python/Streamlit process uses Streamlit communication (WebSocket). rules.py and Session State are inside the same Python process. Bidirectional symbols mean calls/results or reads/writes, not independent services. JSON downloads to the user device. Host grouping does not establish a security trust boundary.

items.title: User
items.body: Operates the browser.

items.title: Browser: user interface
items.body: Input and result display; ↔ Python/Streamlit process.

items.title: Python/Streamlit process
items.body: Run validation and generate reports.

items.title: rules.py: validation rules
items.body: Direct in-process calls and returned results.

items.title: Session State: session memory
items.body: Input and checked snapshots held inside the process; read/write.

items.title: JSON file on the user device
items.body: Browser → download; managed separately from server memory.

en.caption: Figure 5 | Four levels of the C4 model
en.description: Downward arrows mean zooming into structure, not execution order. Use the levels that help answer the question; all four are not always necessary. A container is not necessarily a Docker container.

items.title: C1 · System Context
items.body: Who uses the system? Which external systems cooperate with it?

items.title: C2 · Container
items.body: Which applications, services and data stores exist?

items.title: C3 · Component
items.body: Which functional components exist within an application?

items.title: C4 · Code
items.body: Which classes, functions and code exist within a component?
